passages.original: id enim agnoscunt, septem ex eis delecti, Aurelius , Alypius , Augustinus, Vincentius, Fortunata, Fortunatianus, et Possidius : totidem Donatistæ, Primianus, Petilianus, Emeritus, Montanus, Gaudentius, Adeodatus, et Protasius : atque Iii inter absentes episcopos partis suæ, ut fucum facerent, Felicem quasi urbis Romæ episcopum nominant, licet Catholici Innocentium tunc sedere testentur, ut verum erat, utque probatissimæ fidei annales tradunt, ad annum a partu Virginis quadringentesimum undecimum. Disputatio dividitur in primam cognitionem, secundam, et tertiam. Tertia sexto Idus junias habita est: quo die profertur Marcellini cognitoris sententia, confutatos a Catholicis Donatistas omnium documentorum manifestatione asserentis, ut divi Augustini verbis utar. Hanc sententiam ut emplam a cognitore Catholico et noctu prolatam , calumniose postea Emeritus et quidam pertinaces Donatistæ arguebant: quos Augustinus acutissime refellit ; cui sane laudi esse debet, quod epitomen collationis brevissimam scripsit, ideo utiliorem futuram quia tertiæ cognitionis magna pars, qum hic deficit, necessario indc petenda est.
passages.english: For this they acknowledge: seven were chosen from among them, Aurelius, Alypius, Augustine, Vincentius, Fortunatus, Fortunatianus and Possidius; and as many Donatists, Primianus, Petilianus, Emeritus, Montanus, Gaudentius, Adeodatus and Protasius. And these, among the absent bishops of their party, in order to put up a pretence, name Felix as if he were bishop of the city of Rome, although the Catholics testify that Innocent was then sitting [as bishop], as was true, and as annals of the most approved reliability record, at the year four hundred and eleven from the Virgin's giving birth. The disputation is divided into a first hearing, a second, and a third. The third was held on the sixth day before the Ides of June; on that day the sentence of Marcellinus the judge is delivered, declaring that the Donatists had been refuted by the Catholics through the clear display of all the documents, to use the words of the blessed Augustine. Afterwards Emeritus and certain obstinate Donatists slanderously attacked this sentence as bought from a Catholic judge and delivered by night; Augustine refutes them most acutely. To his credit, indeed, must be counted the fact that he wrote a very brief epitome of the conference, which would prove all the more useful because a large part of the third hearing, which is missing here, must necessarily be sought from there.
passages.notes: 'Fortunata' read as Fortunatus (cf. Fortunatus of Constantina in a later unit). 'Iii' read as 'hi'; 'emplam' as 'emptam' (bought); 'qum' as 'quae'; 'indc' as 'inde'.

passages.original: Cognitorem quidem Orosius libro septimo prudentem, industrium et studiorum bonorum appetentissimum fuisse testatur : ad eumque non multo post Romam captam, scripti sunt ab Augustino libri viginti de Civitate Dei, ut præratio ad eos indicat. De morte autem Marcellini Hieronymus loquitur lib. 3 contra Pelag. violentam eam fuisse necesse est. Percussorem enim ejus et sicarium idem Orosius nominat. Laudandus quoque est Marcellus qui hoc volumen Actorum collationi:, quod copiosissi- mum atque diffusissimum erat, modulata, ut ipse ait, brevitate distinxitatque collegit, ut ex epistola ejus ad Severianum et Julianum videri potest.
passages.english: Orosius, in his seventh book, testifies that the judge was prudent, industrious and most eager for good studies; and to him, not long after the capture of Rome, Augustine's twenty books On the City of God were written, as the preface to them indicates. Jerome speaks of the death of Marcellinus in book 3 against the Pelagians; it must have been violent, for the same Orosius names his assailant and murderer. Praise is also due to Marcellus, who arranged and compiled this volume of the Acts of the conference, which was very copious and very diffuse, with a measured brevity, as he himself says, as can be seen from his letter to Severianus and Julianus.
passages.notes: The text has 'viginti' (twenty); City of God has twenty-two books, but the Latin is translated as it stands. 'praeratio' read as 'praefatio'; 'distinxitatque' as 'distinxit atque'.

passages.original: Gesta collationis Carthaginensis inter episcopos Catholicos et Donatistas quæ nunc exstant, integra non sunt, sed abbreviata ex illis quæ conscripta fuerant coram Marcellino Notario. Nam cum illa valde prolixa essent, ut Augustinus ait in epistola quinquage- sima, timendumque propterea esset ne in contemplum venirent, Severianus et Julianus a Marcello Memo- riali, qui collationi interfuerat et cum Marcellino com municaverat laborem librandæ disceptationis, exegerunt uti fastidia lectionis remedio brevitatis excluderet.
passages.english: The acts of the Carthaginian conference between the Catholic and Donatist bishops that now survive are not complete, but abridged from those that had been written down in the presence of Marcellinus the notary. For since those were very long, as Augustine says in his fiftieth letter, and it was therefore to be feared that they would fall into contempt, Severianus and Julianus required of Marcellus the memorialis, who had been present at the conference and had shared with Marcellinus the labour of weighing the dispute, that he should banish the tedium of reading by the remedy of brevity.
passages.notes: 'contemplum' read as 'contemptum'. *Memorialis* is an office of the imperial secretariat, left as a title.

passages.original: 16, ubi dicitur Profuturi ante paucissimos annos defuncti, in sede Constantiniensi successor. Possidius Calamensis episcopus Augustini fuit discipulus, ab eo Dei verbo nutritus, Donatistarum hostis acerrimus, a quUm, pene interfectus est , ut narrat Augustinus epist. 166. Scripsit Augustini Vitam, in qua testis est se quadraginta annis Dei dono absque amara ulla dissensione familiariter ac dulciter vixisse. Hæc de actoribus catholicis. Cæteri vix aliter noli quam ex præsentibus gestis, ex quibus sedes eorum episcopales collegimus , quod unum de ipsis superest.
passages.english: 16, where he is called successor in the see of Constantina to Profuturus, who had died a very few years before. Possidius, bishop of Calama, was a disciple of Augustine, nourished by him on the word of God, a most fierce enemy of the Donatists, by whom he was nearly killed, as Augustine relates in letter 166. He wrote the Life of Augustine, in which he testifies that by God's gift he lived with him for forty years intimately and pleasantly without any bitter disagreement. So much for the Catholic spokesmen. The others are scarcely known otherwise than from the present acts, from which we have gathered their episcopal sees, which is the one thing about them that remains.
passages.notes: Opens mid-reference (chapter number). 'a quUm' read as 'a quibus'; 'noli' as 'noti'.

passages.original: Donatistarum actoribus quatuor aut quinque celebres sunt : Primianus Parmeniam Donatistæ successor m sede Carthaginensi circa annum Christi 390 , qui statim a Feliciano aliisque suæ partis episcopis damnatus est, et depositus in concilio Cabarsussitano anni 395, subrogato in ejus locum Maximiano : at paulo post in concilio Bagaiensi absolutus et restitutus dejeclo Maximiano. Qua de re centies apud Augustinum fit mentio. Petilianus ante episcopalum forensis advocatus e catechumeno in Catholica, per vim a Donatistis ordinatus episcopus Constantinæ,cujus exstant litteræ, adversum quas Augustinus scripsit.
passages.english: Of the Donatist spokesmen four or five are well known. Primianus, successor of the Donatist Parmenian in the see of Carthage around the year of Christ 390, who was immediately condemned by Felicianus and other bishops of his party and deposed at the council of Cabarsussi in the year 395, Maximianus being put in his place; but shortly afterwards at the council of Bagai he was acquitted and restored, Maximianus being cast out. This is mentioned a hundred times in Augustine. Petilianus, before his episcopate an advocate in the courts, was, while a catechumen in the Catholic [Church], ordained by force by the Donatists as bishop of Constantina; his letters survive, against which Augustine wrote.
passages.notes: 'Parmeniam' read as 'Parmeniani'; 'm sede' as 'in sede'.

passages.original: 246. Interlocutio qua jubetur .ut Augustinus de ordinatore suo ad quæsita respondeat.
passages.english: 246. Ruling by which Augustine is ordered to answer the questions about the one who ordained him.

passages.original: 58. Marcellinus vir clarissimus tribunus et notaris dixit. Has quoque subscriptiones cum mandato gesta suscipient. Et adjecit. Numerus etiam subscribentium designetur. Martialis exceptor dixit. Ducenti sexaginta sex sunt.
passages.english: 58. Marcellinus, of clarissimus rank, tribune and notary, said: "The acts will also receive these signatures together with the mandate." And he added: "Let the number of signatories also be recorded." Martialis the stenographer said: "There are two hundred and sixty-six."

passages.original: 76. Aurelius episcopus Ecclesiæ catholicæ dixit. Nescimus postea quam mandavarunt quid opus erat ut concluderentur. Et alia manu. Recognovi. Augustinus episcopus Ecclesiæ catholicæ dixit. De quorum nomine dubitatur, ipsi veniant. Et alia manu. Recognovi.
passages.english: 76. Aurelius, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: "We do not know, after they had given their mandate, what need there was for them to be shut in." And in another hand: "I have checked it." Augustine, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: "Let those whose names are in doubt come themselves." And in another hand: "I have checked it."
passages.notes: 'concluderentur' may refer to confining the bishops or closing the list; sense uncertain.

passages.original: 78. Augustinus episcopus Ecclesiæ catholicæ dixit. Tumultus ne fieret cavendum fuit, et hoc salubrilcr prudenterque providisti. Et quoniam metuendum est, Me, cum fuerit exorta aliqua perturbatio, nobis potius tribuatur, incertumque sit hominibus, a quorum parte potius exstiterit, nihil melius et tranquillius putamus decernere nobilitatem tuam , nisi ut fecitatis omnibus nominibus, de quo dubitant, veniat.
passages.english: 78. Augustine, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: "Care had to be taken that no uproar should occur, and you have provided for this beneficially and prudently. And since it is to be feared that, if some disturbance should arise, it may be attributed rather to us, and people may be uncertain from which side it arose, we think your nobility can decree nothing better or more peaceable than that, when all the names have been read out, the one about whom they are in doubt should come forward."
passages.notes: 'Me' read as 'ne'; 'fecitatis' as 'recitatis'.

passages.original: 81. Augustinus episcopus Ecclesiæ catholicæ dixit. Ad multa fratris mei videat nobilitas tua quam pauca respondeam. Quod si nobis voluerint respondere , causa tota cito fursitan peragetur; metuendum est , ne ideo non fiat tumultus ab hac turba quæ præsens est, quia non Iiic est alia multitudo, in quam Possit referri causatio.
passages.english: 81. Augustine, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: "Let your nobility see how little I reply to my brother's many points. But if they are willing to answer us, the whole case will perhaps quickly be completed. It is to be feared that an uproar does not arise from this crowd which is present for this reason, that there is not another multitude here onto which the blame could be shifted."
passages.notes: The last sentence is awkward; 'ne ... non' may be corrupt (perhaps 'it is to be feared that an uproar may arise ... because there is no other crowd to blame'). 'Iiic' read as 'hic'.

passages.original: 83. Augustinus episcopus Ecclesiæ caholicæ dixit. Non condteor cum tumultu esse venturos; sed timeo ne ideo adhuc quiescat multitudo praesenS , quia non cst in quem referat si quid forte turbulenter exstite- rit , dum utraque praeses fuerit multitudo.
passages.english: 83. Augustine, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: "I do not claim that they will come with an uproar; but I fear that the crowd now present is quiet for the time being only because there is no one to whom it could be referred, if anything disorderly should perhaps arise, while each crowd was present."
passages.notes: Scanning errors corrected: 'caholicæ' to catholicae, 'condteor' presumably for 'confiteor' (or similar), 'praesenS' to praesens, 'cst' to est. The phrase 'dum utraque praeses fuerit multitudo' is read as 'praesens'; the sense of the last clause is uncertain.

passages.original: 93. Alypius episcopus Ecclesiæ catholicae dixit. Non est dilata causa; hodie agenda est. Et alia manu. Recognovi. Augustinus episcopus dixit. (Mandalum) actis offeratur, ab officio offeratur.
passages.english: 93. Alypius, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: "The case has not been postponed; it is to be dealt with today." And in another hand: "I have checked [it]." Bishop Augustine said: "Let the mandate be submitted to the record; let it be submitted by the office staff."
passages.notes: 'Mandalum' read as 'mandatum'.

passages.original: Sextilius episcopus plebis Assabensis (144). Idem dixit. Præsto sum. Marcianus episcopus [loci suprascripti] dixit. Agnosco illum. Item recitavit. Marcianus episcopus Idicrensis (145). Idem dixit. Praesto sum. Martialis episcopus dixit. Agnosco illum. Item recitavit. Crispulus episcopus Ecclesias Volitanæ (146). Idem dixit. Præsto sum. Quodvultdeus episcopus dixit. Agnosco illum. Item recitavit. Germanus episcopus Gypsariensis (147).
passages.english: Sextilius, bishop of the people of Assaba (144). The same said: "I am present." Marcianus, bishop [of the place named above], said: "I recognise him." He read out again: Marcianus, bishop of Idicra (145). The same said: "I am present." Martialis the bishop said: "I recognise him." He read out again: Crispulus, bishop of the Church of Volita (146). The same said: "I am present." Quodvultdeus the bishop said: "I recognise him." He read out again: Germanus, bishop of Gypsaria (147).
passages.notes: Numbers in parentheses are the edition's note numbers. 'Ecclesias' read as 'Ecclesiae'.

passages.original: Item accedente Felice episcopo 289 Ficense (445), idem dixit. Mando et consentio. Item accedente Felice episcopo Macrianensi, idem dixit. Mando et consentio. Item accedente Lucio episcopo Olivensi (446), idem dixit. Mando et consentio. Item accedente Tertulliano episcopo Hirenensi (147), idem dixit. Mando et consentio. Item accedente Joanne Gummitano (448) episcopo, idem dixit. Mando et consentio. Item accedente Ampelio Vagensi (449) idem dixit. Mando et consentio. Item accedente Primulo episcopo Vagense, idem dixit.
passages.english: Likewise, when Felix, bishop of Ficus (445), came forward, the same said: "I give the mandate and consent." Likewise, when Felix, bishop of Macriana, came forward, the same said: "I give the mandate and consent." Likewise, when Lucius, bishop of Oliva (446), came forward, the same said: "I give the mandate and consent." Likewise, when Tertullianus, bishop of Hirena (447), came forward, the same said: "I give the mandate and consent." Likewise, when John, bishop of Gummi (448), came forward, the same said: "I give the mandate and consent." Likewise, when Ampelius of Vaga (449) came forward, the same said: "I give the mandate and consent." Likewise, when Primulus, bishop of Vaga, came forward, the same said:
passages.notes: '289' is a page number of the printed edition, omitted. Note number '(147)' is evidently a misreading of (447). Place-name forms (Ficus, Hirena, Gummi) are uncertain.

passages.original: 8. Martialis exceptor dixit. Cujusmodi notariam episcopi hesterno nobilitati tuae obtulerint, hanc in manibus habemus : si praecipit nobilitas tua , recitamus.
passages.english: 8. Martialis the stenographer said: "We have in our hands the notice, of whatever kind, which the bishops presented to Your Nobility yesterday; if Your Nobility so orders, we will read it out."
passages.notes: 'notariam' (a written notice) is an unusual term; rendered 'notice'.

passages.original: 14. Augustinus episcopus Ecclesiæ catholicæ dixit. Nos in hoc consensisse litteris nostris expressimus. Et alia manu. Recognovi.
passages.english: 14. Augustine, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: "We have stated in our letter that we agreed to this." And in another hand: "I have checked [it]."

passages.original: 38. Marcellinus vir clarissimus tribunus et notarius dixit. Exceptores, utrum hesterno die omnia potuerint in schedis gesta describi, apud acta designent. Martialis exceptor dixit. Adhuc partem in codicibus habemus. Siquidem etiam ii episcopi qui nobis custodes dati sunt, non nesciunt.
passages.english: 38. Marcellinus, a man of senatorial rank, tribune and notary, said: "Let the stenographers indicate for the record whether all the proceedings of yesterday could be written out on the sheets." Martialis the stenographer said: "We still have part [of it] in the notebooks. Indeed, the bishops who were assigned to us as supervisors are also aware of this."

passages.original: Hæc rectius et justius praeterito judicio debuerant postulari, in quo ex consensu utriusque partis in hunc diem dilata cognitio est. Unde ab ecclesiasticis notariis ad quam partem fuerit dilata cognitio 293 recitetur. Petilianus episcopus dixit. Ergo circum venti sumus. Et alia manu. Ut supra. Augustinus episcopus Ecclesiae catholicæ dixit. Non est nostra causa factum, quod nobis volunt imputare fratres nostri e diverso sistentes. Et cum diceret, (Et alia manu. Recognovi.) Petilianus episcopus dixit. Injuriam nobis facis. Et alia manu. Ut supra.
passages.english: "These [requests] ought more properly and more justly to have been made at the previous hearing, in which, by the agreement of both parties, the inquiry was postponed to this day. Therefore let the church notaries read out at whose instance the inquiry was postponed." Bishop Petilian said: "So we have been tricked." And in another hand: "As above." Augustine, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: "What our brothers standing on the opposite side want to blame on us was not done on our account." And as he was speaking (and in another hand: "I have checked [it]"), Bishop Petilian said: "You are doing us an injury." And in another hand: "As above."
passages.notes: 'ad quam partem' could also mean 'to which party's advantage'. '293' is a page number, omitted.

passages.original: 50. Augustinus episcopus Ecclesiæ catholicte dixit. Edictum nobilitalis tuae sic se habet, quartum mensem concludi ad diem kalendarum iunii. Ante autem nos venimus; et ipsi qui videntur nobis hinc facere invidiam, octavo kalendas Junias mandaverunt: cum utique, si ante diem venerant, ante ipsum diem mandare debuerint.
passages.english: 50. Augustine, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: "Your Nobility's edict states this: that the fourth month closes on the day of the Kalends of June. But we came before that; and those very men who seem to be stirring up ill will against us on this account issued their mandate on the eighth day before the Kalends of June, whereas, if indeed they had come before the day, they ought to have issued the mandate before that very day."

passages.original: 56. Augustinus episcopus Ecclesiæ catholicæ dixit: Hoc solum constet ipsos rem velle differre. Ut concedat sublimitas tua, petimus te. Humanum est, considerare volunt, discutere volunt, paratiores volunt venire, ne nolentes differre prolixiora gesta faciamus, et ipsa gestorum prolixitas majores nobis moras incutiat. Et alia manu. Recognovi.
passages.english: 56. Augustine, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: "Let it simply be established that they themselves want to delay the matter. We ask Your Sublimity to grant it. It is human; they want to consider, they want to discuss, they want to come better prepared; [let it be granted,] so that by refusing to postpone we do not make the proceedings longer, and the very length of the proceedings bring us greater delays." And in another hand: "I have checked [it]."
passages.notes: The construction 'ne nolentes differre...' is compressed; the bracketed supplement reflects the implied sense.

passages.original: 7. Augustinus episcopus Ecclesiæ catholicæ dixit. Principale negotium jamdiu est ut cupimus terminari. Proinde, si vel sero conceditur, probent, quoniam ex parte adversa esse desiderant, totiens objecta Ecclesiæ sanctae catholicæ toto orbe diffusae crimina et numquam probata. Et cum diceret, (Et alia manu. Recognovi.)
passages.english: 7. Augustine, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: It has long been our desire that the principal business be brought to an end. Accordingly, even if it is granted late, let them prove, since they wish to be the opposing party, the charges so often brought against the holy Catholic Church spread throughout the whole world and never proven. And as he was speaking, (And in another hand: I have checked it.)
passages.notes: The final clause "Et cum diceret" appears to be a fragment, perhaps the start of an interruption or misplaced; the sentence is incomplete.

passages.original: 20. Augustinus episcopus Ecclesiæ catholicæ dixit. Si ad rem judicas pertinere, præstantiæ tute eat considerare. Catholicis episcopis vel legatis catholicorum episcororum concessum esse habendam collationem, tenor rescripti imperialis ostėndit. Venimus utrique, hic sumus; et Deus nos disputatores et collatores magis quam litigatores esse praecepit, et ni- hil aliud voluit Deum timens et Deo serviens clementissimus imperator. Adstitisse legitimas personas, et confirmata esse mandata primo die conflictus nostri judicavit sublimitas tua.
passages.english: 20. Augustine, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: If you judge it relevant to the matter, it is for your excellency to consider. The tenor of the imperial rescript shows that the Catholic bishops, or the delegates of the Catholic bishops, were granted the holding of a conference. We have both come; here we are. And God has commanded us to be disputants and conferees rather than litigants, and the most clement emperor, fearing God and serving God, wanted nothing else. Your highness judged on the first day of our contest that the legitimate persons were present and that the mandates were confirmed.
passages.notes: "tute eat" is evidently a scanning error, probably for "tuae est" ("it is for your excellency"); translated accordingly.

passages.original: 29. Martialis exceptor dixit. Inter imperii nostri maximas curas, catholicae legis reverentia aut prima semper aut sola est. Neque enim aliud aut belli laboribus agimus, aut pacis consiliis ordinamus, nisi ut verum Dei cultum orbis nostri plebs devota custo- diat;
passages.english: 29. Martialis the clerk said: "Among the greatest cares of our empire, reverence for the Catholic law is always either the first or the only one. For we do nothing else, whether in the labours of war or in the counsels of peace that we arrange, except that the devout people of our world may keep the true worship of God;
passages.notes: The clerk is reading an imperial rescript; the quotation continues beyond the passage.

passages.original: dO. Augustinus episcopus Ecclesiæ catholicæ dixit. Advertat nobilitas tua quanta aguntur ut nihil agatur. Et alia manu. Recognovi. Montanus episcopus dixit. Ordine integro causa peragenda est. Et alia manu. Montanus episcopus recognovi, salva provocatione.
passages.english: [4]0. Augustine, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: Let your nobility observe how much is being done so that nothing may be done. And in another hand: I have checked it. Bishop Montanus said: The case must be carried through in full order. And in another hand: I, Bishop Montanus, have checked it, without prejudice to appeal.
passages.notes: The section number "dO" is a scanning error, probably for 40.

passages.original: 41. Augustinus episcopus Ecclesia catholicæ dixit. Praesentes sunt, utrique convenimus : locus iste episcopis pene refertus est, mandata recitata atque firmata sunt; non negatur a partibus nostris postulatam esse collationem, ut in ea collatione tandem aliquando vel probent vel probare non potuisse monstrentur, quae solent non nobis , non unicuique nostrum, sed universo orbi christiano objicere crimina : qui Christianus orbis non opinione humana , sed divinis testimoniis et promissus est, et impletur.
passages.english: 41. Augustine, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: They are present; we have both come together; this place is almost filled with bishops; the mandates have been read out and confirmed. It is not denied that the conference was requested by our side, so that in that conference they may at last either prove, or be shown to have been unable to prove, the charges which they are accustomed to bring not against us, not against each one of us, but against the whole Christian world: a Christian world which was both promised, and is being fulfilled, not by human opinion but by divine testimonies.

passages.original: 44. Augustinus episcopus Ecclesiæ catholicæ dixit. Tuae sunt partes, vir nobilis. Si respondit ad ea quae diximus , opus est ut respondeamus. Si autem pervidet praestantia tua nihil eum respondisse ad id quod jusle flagitamus, sed moris superfluis alias moras superfluas addidisse, judica ut videtur.
passages.english: 44. Augustine, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: The part is yours, noble sir. If he has answered what we said, we need to reply. But if your excellency perceives that he has answered nothing to what we justly demand, but has added further needless delays to needless delays, judge as seems [right].

passages.original: 50. Augustinus episcopus Ecclesiæ catholicæ dixit. Legatur mandatum nostrum, et intelligent qnam cuncta contineat. Et alia manu. Recognovi. Petilianus episcopus partis Donati dixit. Patere, præsta judici patientiam quam nobis praestat. Et alia manu. Petilianus episcopus recognovi sine præjudicio appellationis nostræ.
passages.english: 50. Augustine, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: Let our mandate be read, and they will understand how much it contains. And in another hand: I have checked it. Petilian, bishop of the party of Donatus, said: Be patient; show the judge the patience he shows us. And in another hand: I, Bishop Petilian, have checked it, without prejudice to our appeal.

passages.original: 55. Augustinus episcopus Ecclesiæ catholicæ dixit. Collatio petita est a legatis nostris. Lex ipsa hoc continet, qua: ad tuam nobilitatem data est Et alia ,Manu. Recognovi.
passages.english: 55. Augustine, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: The conference was requested by our delegates. The law itself, which was given to your nobility, contains this. And in another hand: I have checked it.

passages.original: 55. Augustinus episcopus ecclesiæ catholicæ dixit. Data est. Omnes fatemur nos petisse collationem, quoniam eam recusabatis; ut tandem sic saltem ad hunc locum vet ad hoc tempus, collationis et dispatationis et demonstrandae veritatis gratia veniremus. Factum est. Venimus, et nihil vultis prodesse quod venimus. Confitemur nos collationem petisse. Nihil aliad imperator quam nos collationem petisse suis verbis expressit.
passages.english: 55. Augustine, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: It was given. We all admit that we requested the conference, because you were refusing it, so that at last, in this way at least, we might come to this place or to this time for the sake of conference, disputation, and the demonstration of the truth. It has been done. We have come, and you want our coming to be of no use. We confess that we requested the conference. The emperor expressed in his own words nothing other than that we requested the conference.
passages.notes: The section number repeats 55 from the previous unit; probably an error for a later number (e.g. 56 or 57).

passages.original: 59. Augustinus episcopus Ecclesiæ o dixit. Si negaremus nos petisse collationem, imperatoris testimonio convinceremur. Habemus imperatorem testem, petisse nos confitemur. Venimus ut fiat quod et nos petivimus, et ille concessit, et adhuc nescio quae dubitationes vel morae interponuntur.
passages.english: 59. Augustine, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: If we denied that we had requested the conference, we would be refuted by the emperor's testimony. We have the emperor as witness; we confess that we requested it. We have come so that there may be done what we both requested and he granted, and still some hesitations or delays or other are being interposed.
passages.notes: "Ecclesiæ o" is a scanning error for "Ecclesiae catholicae".

passages.original: Montanus episcopus salvo provocationis effectu recognovi. Vincentius episcopus Ecclesie catholicæ dixit. Profes. sionem tuam tu superare non potes. Unde recessisti cognosce. Omissa repctere non potes. Et alia manu. Recognovi. Augustinus episcopus Ecclesiæ catholicæ dixit. Quid flagitas quando petierim, cum videas quando venerim? Quid quaeris utrum petierim, cum universum catholicum praesens in hac urbe consilium mandatum dederit, mandato subscripserit, subscriptiones praesens te instante cognoverit ?
passages.english: I, Bishop Montanus, have checked [this], without prejudice to the effect of our appeal. Vincentius, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: You cannot get past your own declaration. Recognise where you have withdrawn from. You cannot go back to what has been passed over. And in another hand: I have checked [this]. Augustine, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: Why do you demand [to know] when I petitioned, when you see when I came? Why do you ask whether I petitioned, when the entire Catholic council, present in this city, gave the mandate, subscribed the mandate, and, being present, verified the subscriptions at your insistence?
passages.notes: 'Profes. sionem' read as 'professionem', 'repctere' as 'repetere'. The sense of 'Unde recessisti cognosce' is uncertain; it may mean 'recognise what you have departed from'.

passages.original: 80. Augustinus episcopus Ecclesiæ catholicæ dixit. Hoc olim clamamus ut fiat. Collatio postulata est, collatio concessa est, causa collationis utrique venimus. Jam tandem fiat, quod et petitum fatemur et concessum esse ipsa concessio declaravit. Et alia manu.
passages.english: 80. Augustine, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: This is what we have long been crying out for, that it should take place. A conference was requested, a conference was granted, and both [sides] have come for the purpose of the conference. Let it now at last take place, since we acknowledge that it was requested, and the grant itself has shown that it was granted. And in another hand:

passages.original: Nos quoque secundum eorum petitionem , ut dicunt, quam nunc in judicio negant, quam approbare nolunt. Et [cum diceret, (Et) alia manu. Emeritus episcopus, salva appellatione nostra, recognovi]. Augustinus episcopus Ecclesiæ catholicæ dixit. Non negamus. Et alia manu. Recognovi. Emeritus episcopus dixit. Quam publicare detrectant, provinciis nostris acciti, conOictum quem se proponere pollicentur, refugere nos non debere omnino profitemur.
passages.english: We too [came] in accordance with their petition, as they say, which they now deny before the court and refuse to prove. And [while he was speaking, (and) in another hand: I, Bishop Emeritus, have checked [this], without prejudice to our appeal]. Augustine, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: We do not deny it. And in another hand: I have checked [this]. Bishop Emeritus said: [The petition] which they decline to make public: summoned from our provinces, we declare that we ought by no means to flee from the contest which they promise to propose.
passages.notes: The passage is disjointed; the opening sentence continues Emeritus' speech from before the passage and lacks a main verb. 'conOictum' read as 'conflictum'. The construction of 'Quam publicare detrectant' is unclear.

passages.original: Magnis actum est voluminibus, et respondere noluerunt, tenentes apud se quodam praejudicio voluntatem, ne satisfacerent judicatis. Et cum diceret. ( Et alia manu. Emeritus episcopus, salva appellatione recognovi. Augustinus episcopus Ecclesiæ catholicæ dixit. Quibus judicatis? Et alia manu. Recognovi. Emeritus episcopus dixit. Vel illud reverentiae ac patientiæ judiciorum prestare dignentur [ut respondeant] utrum petitoris loco adsistant, utrum ipsi proponant , utrum ipsi nos in judicium vocent;
passages.english: It was dealt with in large volumes, and they refused to answer, holding their intention within themselves by a kind of prejudgment, so as not to comply with what has been decided. And while he was speaking (and in another hand: I, Bishop Emeritus, have checked [this], without prejudice to the appeal), Augustine, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: What decisions? And in another hand: I have checked [this]. Bishop Emeritus said: Let them at least deign to show this much reverence and patience toward the proceedings, [that they answer] whether they stand in the place of petitioner, whether they themselves are making the case, whether they themselves are summoning us to court;
passages.notes: The parenthesis opened after 'Et cum diceret' is not closed in the text. 'judicatis' could mean 'what has been decided' or 'the judges' decisions'.

passages.original: 98. Augustinus episcopus Ecclesiæ catholicæ dixit. Ecclesia, quod audire non vultis, et necesse est audiatis, quoniam tot testimoniis et divinis eloquiis proclamatur toto terrarum orbe diffusa, cujus communionem. videmur tenere, falsis criminationibus a vo- bis appetita est. Unde exstitit vestra separatio, quam dolemus. Istae criminationes quibus insectari soletis Ecclesiam toto, sicut promissa est, orbe diffusam, hodie audire volumus utrum verae sint.
passages.english: 98. Augustine, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: The Church, something you do not want to hear and must hear, since it is proclaimed by so many testimonies and divine oracles to be spread over the whole world, the Church whose communion we are seen to hold, has been attacked by you with false accusations. From this arose your separation, which we grieve over. These accusations, with which you usually assail the Church spread over the whole world as it was promised, we want to hear today, [to learn] whether they are true.

passages.original: Intelligant e diverso venientes propositionibus nostris se respondere debere, ut adstantes aot non adstantes, quid personæ gerant dicere non morentur, ut eorum intentionibus respondere valeamus. Et alia manu. Emeritus episcopus, salvo 302 effectu appellationis nostræ, recognovi. Marcellinus vir clarissimus tribunus et notarius dixit. Quid refertur? Augustinus episcopus Ecclesiæ catholicæ dixit. Personas primo die Judicii esse firmatas et sequenti etiam die interlocu- tionis tuæ. Et cum diceret (Et alia manu. Recognovi.) Marcellinus vir clarissimus tribunus et notarius dixit. Aliud quæsitum est.
passages.english: Let those who come from the opposite side understand that they must answer our propositions, so that, whether they stand [as petitioners] or not, they may not delay to say what role they are playing, so that we may be able to answer their claims. And in another hand: I, Bishop Emeritus, have checked [this], without prejudice to the effect of our appeal. Marcellinus, a man of senatorial rank, tribune and notary, said: What is being put forward? Augustine, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: That the parties were established on the first day of the proceedings, and on the following day also by your interlocutory ruling. And while he was speaking (and in another hand: I have checked [this]), Marcellinus, a man of senatorial rank, tribune and notary, said: Something else was asked.
passages.notes: 'aot' read as 'aut'; '302' is a page number and has been omitted. 'adstantes' probably refers to standing in the role of petitioner.

passages.original: 100. Augustinus episcopus Ecclesiæ catholicce dixit. Interlocationis tuae forma declaravit. Sed quia dicit cum peregrinis Christianis non se habere aliquam rationem, sed hoc totum quod agitur, inter At'ros agi, Afrorum Christianornm Catholicorum hæc vox est :. Nos universo orbi Christiano communione cohæremus. Hanc Ecclesiam elegimus retinendam, quam in eis scripturis invenimus. [Et cum diceret.] Et ( alia manu.
passages.english: 100. Augustine, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: The wording of your interlocutory ruling has made [this] clear. But since he says that he has no dealings with foreign Christians, and that this whole matter being dealt with is dealt with among Africans, this is the voice of the African Catholic Christians: We are united in communion with the whole Christian world. We have chosen to keep this Church, the one that we find in those scriptures. [And while he was speaking.] And (in another hand:
passages.notes: 'Interlocationis' read as 'interlocutionis', 'At'ros' as 'Afros'. 'in eis scripturis' ('in those scriptures') seems to lack an expected qualifier such as 'holy', or may be corrupt.

passages.original: 101. Augustinus episcopus Ecclesiæ catholicæ dixit. Nos eam Ecclesiam retinemus, quam in illis scripturis invenimus, in quibus etiam cognovimus Christum. Scripturae quippe nostrae, quarum auctorilati utrique subdimur, Christum et Ecclesiam tamquam sanctum commendant conjugium, Christum sponsum, illam sponsam. Ubi illum cognoscimus, ibi et Illam invenire debemus. Si itaque nunc exorti essemus, et cogitaremus in Africa cui communioni Christiano.
passages.english: 101. Augustine, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: We hold to that Church which we find in those Scriptures in which we have also come to know Christ. For our Scriptures, to whose authority both [sides] submit, commend Christ and the Church as a holy marriage, Christ the bridegroom, she the bride. Where we come to know him, there we ought also to find her. So if we had only now come into being, and were considering in Africa to which communion of Christians
passages.notes: The sentence breaks off mid-word (Christiano-/rum); it continues in the following passage.

passages.original: 108. Augustinus episcopus Ecclesiæ catholicæ dixit. Tuæ sublimitatis est judicare, nos ad eorum criminationes refellendas ingressi sumus. Solent Ecde- siam quam tenemus crimine traditionis arguere. Et alia manu. Recognovi.
passages.english: 108. Augustine, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: It is for Your Highness to judge; we have come in to refute their accusations. They usually charge the Church which we hold with the crime of *traditio* [the handing over of the scriptures in persecution]. And in another hand: I have checked [this].

passages.original: 110. Augustinus episcopus Ecclesiæ catholicæ dixit. Solent Ecclesiae quam tenemus crimina traditionis objicere, et nescio quorum peccatis eam contendere esse destructam et exstinctam. Et alia manu. Reoognovi. Emeritus episcopus dixit. Non hoc a te petii. Fac satis judicatis. Et alia manu. Emeritus episcopus salvo effectu appellationis recognovi. Augustinus episcopus Ecclesiæ catholice dixit.
passages.english: 110. Augustine, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: They usually charge the Church which we hold with the crimes of *traditio* [the handing over of the scriptures in persecution], and contend that it has been destroyed and extinguished by the sins of who knows whom. And in another hand: I have checked [this]. Bishop Emeritus said: I did not ask this of you. Comply with what has been decided. And in another hand: I, Bishop Emeritus, have checked [this], without prejudice to the effect of the appeal. Augustine, bishop of the Catholic Church, said:

passages.original: 116. Augustinus episcopus Ecclesiæ catholicæ dixit. Nos collationem poposcimus ubi objecta diluamus, non ubi objiciamus diluenda; quandoquidem cum illi objecta probare non potuerint, quid sint, quid remaneant, nobis non dicentibus manifestum erit omninibus, et a tua sublimitate judicabitur. Nunc ingressi sumus diluere criminationes eorum, quas solent Ecclesiæ quam tenemus objicere: mandatum quoque ipsorum hoc continet.
passages.english: 116. Augustine, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: We requested a conference at which we might clear away the charges, not one at which we might make charges to be cleared away. For when they have been unable to prove their charges, what they are and what they are left as will be plain to all without our saying it, and it will be judged by Your Highness. Now we have come in to clear away their accusations, which they usually make against the Church which we hold. Their own mandate also contains this:
passages.notes: 'omninibus' read as 'omnibus'. 'quid sint, quid remaneant' is obscure; it probably means 'what [the accusers] are and what they remain'.

passages.original: Concedere non possum ut ea quæ velunt in judicio ventilent, nisi ea quæ de ipsis flagitavi in judicio deprompserint. Et alia manu. Adcodatus episcopus prosecutionem meam salva appellatione recognovi. Augustinus episcopus Ecclesiæ catholicæ dixit. Nos ista de archivis accepimus. Si quid est quod et tu accipere potuisti, si recitandum poposceris, et a nobis fuerit contradictum, iniquos deputa, et vicem redde. Et alia manu. Recognovi.
passages.english: I cannot agree that they should air in the hearing what they wish, unless they produce in the hearing what I have demanded of them. And in another hand: I, Bishop Adeodatus, have checked my statement, with my right of appeal reserved. Augustine, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: We received these [documents] from the archives. If there is anything that you too have been able to obtain, if you ask for it to be read and we object, count us unfair and pay [us] back in kind. And in another hand: I have checked [it].
passages.notes: "Adcodatus" is a scanning error for Adeodatus; "velunt" read as "volunt".

passages.original: 155. Augustinus episcopus Ecclesiæ catholicæ dixit. Ad ca quae prosecuta est modo pars diversa, paucis advertat sublimitas tua. Nos Ecclesiam catholicam retinere, ipsa nostrae communionis testificatione monstramus, quam Ecclesiam probare descendimus, si permittant, non rumoribus humanis, neque errantibus opinionibus, sed divinis eloquiis declaratam. Ut autem leges, vel gesta, vel quæcumque de archivis prolata offeramus in hac collatione recitanda, ipsi cogunt qui talibus agunt.
passages.english: 155. Augustine, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: To what the opposing party has just stated, let Your Sublimity attend briefly. That we hold the Catholic Church we show by the very testimony of our communion, a Church which we have come down [here] to prove, if they allow [it], as declared not by human rumours, nor by wandering opinions, but by the divine utterances. But that we offer laws, or records, or whatever has been brought out of the archives, to be read in this conference, those who proceed by such means force [us to do].

passages.original: 160. Augustinus episcopus Ecclesiæ catholicæ dixit. Jam toties conclamavimus. Mandatum quod injunctum est legatis episcoporum , ab episcopis flagitant sibi recitari. Hoc est aliena requirere ad causam non pertinentia. Mandatum quod nobis propter collationem cum his faciendam injunctum est, hoc recilatum est, hoc eis sufficiat. Quid si enim aliqua legatis mandata sunt, ad causam quidem istam non pertinentia, sed quae ipsos scire nolumus ?
passages.english: 160. Augustine, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: We have already cried out so many times. They demand that the mandate entrusted to the envoys of the bishops be read to them by the bishops. This is to seek out other people's business that does not pertain to the case. The mandate that was entrusted to us for holding the conference with them, this has been read; let this suffice them. For what if some things were entrusted to the envoys which do not indeed pertain to this case, but which we do not want them to know?

passages.original: 162. Augustinus episcopus Ecclesiæ catholice dixit. Non hoc dixi, non advertisti , aut dissimul as te audisse quod dixi. Audi, planius hoc dicimus, ne forte culpa mea non intellexeris, dum id obscurius aliquantum dixi studio brevitatis, quod percipere nequiveris. Notum est omnibus multas causas habere Ecclesiam, et suam, et privatarum personarum sibimet commissarum; et potest fieri ut ad episcopo. rum intercessionem multa pertineant.
passages.english: 162. Augustine, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: I did not say this; you did not pay attention, or you pretend to have heard what I said. Listen, we say this more plainly, lest perhaps through my fault you did not understand, since I said it somewhat obscurely out of a desire for brevity, so that you were unable to grasp [it]. It is known to all that the Church has many cases, both its own and those of private persons entrusted to it; and it can happen that many matters pertain to the intercession of bishops.

passages.original: 176. Augustinus episcopus Ecclesiæ catholicæ dixit. Hæc postulavimus, sed præcedentibus vestris criminationibus et accusationibus. Nam proferimus antiquissima gesta, quibus vestri majores tunc in tempore ad Anulinum venerunt proconsulem , et illi chartas in qmbus dicerent majorum nostrorum crimina esse conscripta obtulerunt, et rogaverunt ut easdem ad Constantinum imperatorem misisset.
passages.english: 176. Augustine, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: We asked for these things, but [only] after your charges and accusations had come first. For we are bringing forward very ancient records, in which your predecessors came at that time to the proconsul Anulinus, and presented papers in which they said the crimes of our predecessors were written down, and asked that he send them to the emperor Constantine.

passages.original: Si autem annosas, antiquasque chartulas cupiunt recitare, habeo pro me validas præscriptiones, recito illud tempus cujus contestatione praetermissionem interim feci. Lapsum causa incurrit, non potest rursus audiri. Et alia manu. Petilianus episcopus salva appellatione recognovi. Augustinus episcopus Ecclesiæ catholicæ dixit. Crimina traditionis objiciunt. Et alia manu. Recognovi. Petilianus epi-A scopus dixit. Hoc causæ est. Et alia manu. Petilianus episcopus salva appellatione recognovi. Augustinus episcopus Ecclesias catholicæ dixit.
passages.english: But if they wish to read old and ancient papers, I have strong pleas in bar on my side; I cite that period by whose attestation I meanwhile made an objection of lapse. The case has incurred lapse; it cannot be heard again. And in another hand: I, Bishop Petilian, have checked [it], with my right of appeal reserved. Augustine, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: They bring charges of handing over [the Scriptures]. And in another hand: I have checked [it]. Bishop Petilian said: This is [the matter] of the case. And in another hand: I, Bishop Petilian, have checked [it], with my right of appeal reserved. Augustine, bishop of the Catholic Church, said:
passages.notes: The sense of "recito illud tempus cujus contestatione praetermissionem interim feci" is uncertain; it seems to refer to a plea of time-limit (praescriptio temporis). "Traditio" is the surrender of the Scriptures in persecution. "epi-A scopus": the A is a printed margin mark.

passages.original: 186. Marcellinus vir clarissimus tribunus et notarius dixit. Respondeatur objeclis. Augustinus episcopus Ecclesiæ catholicæ dixit. Si patiantur, Ecclesiæ quam tenemus (sicut omnes noverunt, quorum solent animos suis sollicitare criminationibus, et etiam sui mandati tenore declararunt); Ecclesiæ , inquam , quam tenemus, crimina solent traditionis objicere. Et alia manu. Recognovi. Petilianus episcopus partis Donati dixit. Profiteantur ad quæsita. Professionem petivimus, non conflictum. Et alia manu. Pelilianus episcopus appellatione incolumi recognovi.
passages.english: 186. Marcellinus, a man of clarissimus rank, tribune and notary, said: Let reply be made to the objections. Augustine, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: If they allow [it]: against the Church which we hold (as all know whose minds they are accustomed to stir up with their accusations, and as they have also declared by the wording of their own mandate), against the Church, I say, which we hold, they are accustomed to bring charges of handing over. And in another hand: I have checked [it]. Petilian, bishop of the party of Donatus, said: Let them make a declaration on the questions put. We asked for a declaration, not a fight. And in another hand: I, Bishop Petilian, have checked [it], with my right of appeal intact.

passages.original: 187. Augustinus episcopus Ecclesiæ catholicæ dixit. Si horum criminum jacturam faciunt, de chartis publicis nihil proferimus. Si autem in eadem criminatione persistunt, chartis publicis docemus hanc causam olim esse Rimam, nec tamen eos ab hujus- modi objiciendis criminibus cessavisse. Unde nunc collationem istam poposcimus, non ut illam causam traditionis quam Cæciliano et ejus collegis objicicbant, suscipiamus denuo finiendam, sed demonstremus olim esse finitam, ut hoc cognoscentes populi qui nesciunt, et istorum adhuc criminationibus commoventur, tandem aliquando cognoscant in qua Ecclesia christianae salutis viam requirant.
passages.english: 187. Augustine, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: If they abandon these charges, we bring forward nothing from the public records. But if they persist in the same accusation, we show from the public records that this case was settled long ago, and yet that they have not ceased from bringing charges of this kind. Hence we have now requested this conference, not in order to take up again for settlement that case of surrender [of the scriptures] which they used to bring against Caecilian and his colleagues, but to demonstrate that it was settled long ago, so that the peoples who do not know this, and are still disturbed by these men's accusations, learning it, may at last know in which Church they should seek the way of Christian salvation.
passages.notes: "Rimam" read as "finitam" ("settled"). "traditio" refers to surrender of scriptures during persecution.

passages.original: 189. Augustinus episcopus Ecclesiæ catholicae dixit. Si petiloris loco adsistunt qui crimina objecta defendunt, tuae nobilitatis est pronuntiare. Et alia manu. Recognovi.
passages.english: 189. Augustine, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: Whether those who defend against the charges brought stand in the position of plaintiff is for Your Nobility to pronounce. And in another hand: I have checked [it].

passages.original: 197. Augustinus episcopus Ecclesiæcatholicæ dixit. Jam diximus unde agamus potius, id est, utrum publicis documentis an divinis testimoniis. In vestra est positum potestate. Si enim a criminibus hominum cessatis, et nos cessabimus a publicis documentis, et solam Ecclesiae causam divinis testimoniis asseremus.
passages.english: 197. Augustine, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: We have already said from what [basis] we should rather proceed, that is, whether from public documents or from divine testimonies. It is placed in your power. For if you leave off the crimes of men, we too shall leave off public documents, and shall maintain the cause of the Church alone by divine testimonies.

passages.original: 199. Augustinus episcopus Ecclesiæ catholice dixit. Ergo ad interrogata respondete. Receditis a criminibus traditionis? Respondeant ad breve inter- rogatum nostrum. Facitis jacturam criminum quae soletis objicere Cæciliano et collegis ejus, an in eadem criminatione persistitis ?
passages.english: 199. Augustine, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: Then answer the questions. Do you withdraw from the charges of handing over? Let them answer our short question. Do you abandon the charges which you are accustomed to bring against Caecilian and his colleagues, or do you persist in the same accusation?

passages.original: 201. Augustinus episcopus Ecclesiae catholicæ dixit. 0 breve responsum ! Quam multum dicitur, ubi inveniri non potest quid dicatur! Breviter respondi ego postulationibus tuis. Voluisti ex me scire, utrum legalibus testimoniis divinis agam, an publicis gestis.
passages.english: 201. Augustine, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: O short answer! How much is said where what is being said cannot be found! I answered your demands briefly. You wanted to learn from me whether I am proceeding by the divine testimonies of the law, or by public records.
passages.notes: "legalibus testimoniis divinis" is awkward. It may mean "the divine testimonies of the law", i.e. the Scriptures.

passages.original: 204. Augustinus episcopus Ecclesiæ catholicæ dixit. Si die decimo quinto venerunt, ut ad quartumdecimum occurrerent, quare octavo kalendas constiterunt ? Et alia manu. Recognovi.
passages.english: 204. Augustine, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: If they came on the fifteenth day so as to be present for the fourteenth, why did they make their formal appearance on the eighth day before the Kalends? And in another hand: I have checked [this].
passages.notes: The dating is obscure without the surrounding debate.

passages.original: 214. Augustinus episcopus Ecclesia: catholicæ dixit. Sed causam Ecclesiæ, non causam Cacciliani et collegarum ejus, quibus crimina intenditis. Ecce pollicemur, et totiens pollicemur quotiens exactum fuerit a nobis, et cum non exigitur, offerimus, Ecclesiæ causam non nisi divinis teslirnoniis firmantus, docemus, ostendimus ;
passages.english: 214. Augustine, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: But [we speak of] the case of the Church, not the case of Caecilian and his colleagues, against whom you bring charges. See, we promise, and we promise as often as it is demanded of us, and when it is not demanded we offer: the case of the Church we establish, teach and show by nothing but divine testimonies;
passages.notes: Scanning errors corrected: "Cacciliani" read as Caeciliani, "teslirnoniis firmantus" as testimoniis firmamus.

passages.original: 218. Augustinus episcopus Ecclesiæ catholicæ dixit. Legat, cl tunc de nobis exigat hujus lectionis firmitatem. Et alia manu. Recognovi.
passages.english: 218. Augustine, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: Let him read, and then let him demand of us the validity of this reading. And in another hand: I have checked [this].
passages.notes: "cl" read as "et".

passages.original: 220. Augustinus episcopus Ecclesiæ catholicæ dixit. Si inde dubitant, archiva proconsulis requirantur. Et alia manu. Recognovi. Marcellinus vir clarissimus tribunus et notarius dixit. Quoniam in arcbivis publicis ea quae recitantur inesse dixisti, sicut cœperat officium, omnia relegerc debebit. Martialis exceptor. ex superioribus gestis recitavit. Eosdemque hortata est , ut unitate consensu omnium facta [cum omni omnino] munere [ indulgentia] Majestatis vestræ Iiberati esse videantur, Catholica custodita, sanctitati legis debita reverentia, ac divinis rebus inserviant.
passages.english: 220. Augustine, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: If they have doubts about it, let the proconsul's archives be searched. And in another hand: I have checked [this]. Marcellinus, a man of senatorial rank, tribune and notary, said: Since you have said that what is being read out is contained in the public archives, the office staff will have to reread everything, as it had begun. Martialis, the clerk, read from the earlier records: "And she urged the same men that, once unity had been achieved by the consent of all, they might be seen to have been freed [with every] privilege [by the indulgence] of Your Majesty, the Catholic [Church] being preserved and due reverence being paid to the sanctity of the law, and that they should devote themselves to divine service."
passages.notes: The quoted document (apparently a proconsul's report to the emperor) is fragmentary. The subject of "hortata est" is feminine and unexpressed, perhaps "Your Majesty" or an earlier feminine noun. The bracketed words are the edition's.

passages.original: 222. Augustinus episcopus Ecclesiæ catholicæ dixit. Ne vobis dicatis patrem in terra , simul audivimus, simul legimus, simul populis prædicamus. Quid de me quæris utrum sim filius Cæciliani ? Caecilianus, si innocens fuit, gaudeat de sua innocentia, me congaudente, non in ejus innocentia me spem meam ponente. Si autem nocens fuit, quod fortasse discussa causa vel sic, vel aliter declarabit, sustinuit eum Ecclesia quam teneo, ut a similitudinibus dominicis non recedam, sicut paleam in aren, sicut in eisdem pascuis hædos, sicut in eisdem retibus pisces malos;
passages.english: 222. Augustine, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: "Do not call [anyone] on earth your father": we have heard it together, read it together, preach it together to the peoples. Why do you ask me whether I am a son of Caecilian? If Caecilian was innocent, let him rejoice in his innocence, and I rejoice with him, but I do not place my hope in his innocence. But if he was guilty, which perhaps the examination of the case will show one way or another, the Church which I hold has borne with him, so that I may not depart from the Lord's similitudes: like chaff on the threshing floor, like goats in the same pastures, like bad fish in the same nets;
passages.notes: Allusion to Matthew 23:9; "aren" read as "area".

passages.original: 226. Augustinus episcopus Ecclesiæ catholicæ dixit. Cæciliani causam vel collegarum ejus solent ipsi Eoclesiæ catholicæ objicere, vel ut sine controversia loquar, ipsi Ecclesiae quam tenemus. Proinde, ut video, magnum volunt adferre compendium. Si hanc causam non objiciunt Ecclesiæ quam tenemus, dicant quid ei objiciant. Si enim nihil, quare separamur? Si aliquid præter causam Cæciliani, idipsum offerant, id ostendant.
passages.english: 226. Augustine, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: They are accustomed to bring the case of Caecilian or his colleagues as a charge against the Catholic Church itself, or, to speak without controversy, against the very Church which we hold. So, as I see it, they want to bring a great shortcut. If they do not bring this case against the Church which we hold, let them say what they charge it with. For if nothing, why are we separated? If something besides the case of Caecilian, let them present that very thing, let them show it.

passages.original: 228. Augustinus episcopus Ecclesiæ catholicæ dixit. Ego in Ecclesia sum in qua Cæcilianus fuit. Et alia manu. Recognovi.
passages.english: 228. Augustine, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: I am in the Church in which Caecilian was. And in another hand: I have checked [this].

passages.original: 230. Augustinus episcopus Ecclesiæ catholicae dixit. In Ecclesia sumus, in qua Cxcilianus episcopatum gessit et diem obiit. Ejus uomen ad altare recitamus, ejus memoriae communicamus, tanquam memoriae fratris, non tanquam patris aut matris. Quaeris autem a me unde communio mea sumat exordium. Dominus ipse Christus asserit exordium communionis meæ dicens: Oportebat Christum pati et resurgere a mortuis tertio die, et prædicari in nomine ejus pœnitentiam ct remissionem peccatorum per omnes gentes, incipientibus ab Hierusalem.
passages.english: 230. Augustine, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: We are in the Church in which Caecilian held the episcopate and died. We recite his name at the altar, we are in communion with his memory as the memory of a brother, not as of a father or a mother. But you ask me where my communion takes its beginning. The Lord Christ himself declares the beginning of my communion, saying: "It was necessary for the Christ to suffer and to rise from the dead on the third day, and for repentance and forgiveness of sins to be preached in his name among all nations, beginning from Jerusalem."

passages.original: 232. Augustinus episcopus Ecclesiae catholicæ dixit. Jam audisti quia frater erat. Et alia manu. Recognovi. Petilianus episcopus dixit. Frater non est qui generat filios. Et alia manu. Petilianus episcopus appellatione incolumi recognovi.
passages.english: 232. Augustine, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: You have already heard that he was a brother. And in another hand: I have checked [this]. Bishop Petilian said: He who begets sons is not a brother. And in another hand: I, Bishop Petilian, have checked [this], without prejudice to [my] appeal.
passages.notes: "appellatione incolumi" is taken as a reservation of the right to appeal.

passages.original: 233. Marcellinus vir clarissimus tribunus et notarius dixit. Nec patrem nec matrem sibi esse Cæcilianum apertissima prosecutione signavit. Augustinus episcopus Ecclesiæ catholicæ dixit. Cæcilianus non est pater meus. Si bonus est, frater meus est bonus; si malus est, frater est malus. Tamen propter sacramenta frater est, sive bonus, sive malus. Et alia manu. Recognovi, Marcellinus vir clarissimus tribunus et notarius dixit.
passages.english: 233. Marcellinus, a man of senatorial rank (*vir clarissimus*), tribune and notary, said: He has indicated with a perfectly clear statement that Caecilian is neither his father nor his mother. Augustine, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: Caecilian is not my father. If he is good, he is my good brother; if he is bad, he is a bad brother. Yet on account of the sacraments he is a brother, whether good or bad. And in another hand: I have checked [it]. Marcellinus, a man of senatorial rank, tribune and notary, said:
passages.notes: "Et alia manu. Recognovi" records each speaker's signed verification of the minutes; the passage ends at the start of Marcellinus' next speech.

passages.original: 235. Augustinus episcopus Ecclesiæ catholicæ dixit. Ecce dico, quoties voluerint dico, Cæcilianus non est pater meus, quia audio Dominum meum dicentem : Ne vobis patrem dicatis in terra: unus est pater vester Deus. Dico Cæcilianum fratrem, bonum fratrem, si bonus; malum fratrem, si malus est, quo. niam propter communia sacrameuta frater meus est. Si autem judicium de illo mcum vis audire, etiam innocentem credo, appetitum falsis criminationibus existimo, sed tamquam homo de homine existimans, non tamquam certum aliquid credens.
passages.english: 235. Augustine, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: See, I say it, I say it as often as they wish: Caecilian is not my father, because I hear my Lord saying: "Do not call [anyone] your father on earth: one is your Father, God." I call Caecilian a brother: a good brother, if he is good; a bad brother, if he is bad, since he is my brother on account of the sacraments we share. But if you want to hear my judgement about him, I even believe him innocent; I consider that he was assailed with false accusations, but [I say this] as one man judging of another, not as believing something certain.
passages.notes: Scanning errors corrected: "quo. niam", "sacrameuta", "mcum".

passages.original: 257. Augustinus episcopus Ecclesiae catholicae dixit. Habeo caput, sed Christus est. Marcellinus vir clarissimus tribunus et notarius dixit. Diligentius demonstretur 312 utrum patrem vestrum Caecilianum,aut matrem, sicut quæsitum est, esse dicatis. Augustinus episcopus Ecclesiæ Catholicce dixit. Habeo caput, sed Christus est, cnjus Apostolum audio.
passages.english: 257. Augustine, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: I have a head, but it is Christ. Marcellinus, a man of senatorial rank, tribune and notary, said: Let it be shown more carefully whether you say that Caecilian is your father or your mother, as was asked. Augustine, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: I have a head, but it is Christ, whose Apostle I hear.
passages.notes: "312" is a page number of the printed edition, omitted.

passages.original: Recognovi), Adeodatus episcopus dixit. Hoc est indicium causie desperatæ, ut cum nos flagitemus alia, alia respondeantur; ut quoniam objectis respondere non possunt, quærant alia quibus nebulas in- .nectant. nectant. Dicat igitur Augustinus quis cum ordinaverit. Et alia manu. Adeodatus episcopus salva appellatione recognovi. Augustinus episcopus Ecclesiæ catholicæ dixit. Superflua quaeri video. Et cum diceret. ( Et alia manu. Rccognovi),
passages.english: I have checked [it]), Adeodatus the bishop said: This is the sign of a hopeless case: that when we demand some things, other things are given in reply; that since they cannot answer the charges, they look for other things with which to weave fogs. Let Augustine, then, say who ordained him. And in another hand: I, Adeodatus the bishop, have checked [it], my appeal reserved. Augustine, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: I see superfluous things being asked. And while he was speaking (and in another hand: I have checked [it]),
passages.notes: "causie" read as "causae"; the duplicated "nectant" and "cum" for "eum" corrected.

passages.original: 247. Augustinus episcopus Ecclesiœ catholicœ dixit. Superflua quæri video a fratribus nostris e diverso sistentibus; et ad ipsa superflua non denego responsionem, dum tamen Ecclesiæ causa, cui responderi nihil potest, in fundamento tutissimo conlocetur. Ego, cujus ordinatorem requiris homo sum Christianus, Metis, quod Deo teste loquor, Catholicus. Unde. adhuc ambigimus quis dignus hoc nomine vocitetur. Ego illam Ecclesiam defendo, hanc assero qualicumque voce, in qua quidquid fuero, illa Ecclesia est.
passages.english: 247. Augustine, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: I see superfluous things being asked by our brothers standing on the opposing side; and I do not refuse an answer even to those superfluous things, provided that the cause of the Church, to which no answer can be made, is set on the safest foundation. I, whose ordainer you ask about, am a Christian man, and, as I say with God as witness, a Catholic. Hence we are still in dispute about who deserves to be called by this name. I defend that Church, I maintain this one with whatever voice [I have], in which, whatever I may turn out to be, that Church is [the Church].
passages.notes: "Metis" is evidently corrupt; perhaps "et" or "fidelis"; rendered as "and". The sense of the final sentence is uncertain.

passages.original: 256. Augustinus episcopus Ecclesiæ catholicæ dixit. Ipsi Iugant. Concedamus eis quod ipsi nobis concedere noluerunt. Marcellinus vir clarissimus tribunus et notarius dixit. Ecclesiastici notarii ea relegant, ut apertius designetur, quae a venerabilibus viris constit oblata. Possidius episcopus Ecclesiæ catholicæ dixit. Scriptum sit ipsos petisse, ut a suis notariis gusta quæ proferunt recitentur.
passages.english: 256. Augustine, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: They themselves [are the ones who] read. Let us grant them what they themselves refused to grant us. Marcellinus, a man of senatorial rank, tribune and notary, said: Let the church notaries read these again, so that what has been submitted by the venerable men may be indicated more clearly. Possidius, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: Let it be written that they themselves asked that what they produce be read out by their own notaries.
passages.notes: "Iugant" is corrupt, probably "legunt"; "constit" read as "constat" ("what is agreed to have been submitted"); "gusta" read as "ista".

passages.original: 261. Augustinus episcopus Ecclesiæ catholicæ dixit. Permitte no, vir sublimi , pro causa Ecclesiæ non diutius superfluis immorari. Atque utinam fratres nostri e diverso sistentes hanc epistolam ante tUos omnes moratorios sermones suos protulissent,, ut jam de Ecclesia, unde causa vertitur, aliquid ageremus, Animadvertit ergo nobilitas tua in hac epistola. duo quædam genera vel objectionum yel rerum inserta quibus respondere debeamus, unum de divinis scripturis et sanctæ legis eloquiis , alterum de criminationibus humanis, quæ objicienda nescio qui invidiosius potius quam verius putaverunt.
passages.english: 261. Augustine, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: Allow me, eminent sir, not to linger any longer on superfluous matters, for the sake of the Church's cause. And would that our brothers standing on the opposing side had produced this letter before all their delaying speeches, so that we might already be dealing somewhat with the Church, on which the case turns. Your Nobility therefore notices that in this letter two kinds of objections, or matters, are included, to which we must answer: one concerning the divine Scriptures and the utterances of the holy law, the other concerning human accusations, which some people or other thought should be raised more out of malice than truth.
passages.notes: Scanning errors corrected: "no" for "me", "tUos" for "tot" ("all these delaying speeches"), "yel" for "vel".

passages.original: 262. Emeritus epistopus dixit. Non legit aream. Et alia manu. Emeritus episcopus recognovi. Augustinus episcopus Ecclesiæ catholicæ dixit. Joannes dixit : Mundabit aream suam, frumenta recondet in horreo (Matth. III , 12; et, Luc, III, 17). Et cum diceret (Et aUa manu Recognovi), Marcellinus vir clarissimus tribunus et notarius dixit. Hoc quod postulat relegatur.
passages.english: 262. Emeritus the bishop said: He did not read [the passage about] the threshing floor. And in another hand: I, Emeritus the bishop, have checked [it]. Augustine, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: John said: "He will clean his threshing floor, he will store the grain in the barn" (Matt. 3:12; and Luke 3:17). And while he was speaking (and in another hand: I have checked [it]), Marcellinus, a man of senatorial rank, tribune and notary, said: Let what he requests be read again.

passages.original: 264. Augustinus episcopus Ecclesiæ catholicæ dixit. Prosecutio postra pro ipsorum epistota habeatur Legi coepit, nullus a nobis relatus est strepitus Nulla interturbatio , nulla interruptio. Permittat ut finiam quod cæpi eloqui, et sip respondeat. Quare non nobis rependitur quod prærogavimus. Anhnadvertit nobilius tua patientiam nostram cum tam longa recitaremur epistola. Et cum diceret (Et alta manu.
passages.english: 264. Augustine, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: Let our statement be taken in return for their letter. It began to be read; no noise was made by us, no disturbance, no interruption. Let him allow me to finish what I began to say, and then let him answer. Why is what we granted in advance not repaid to us? Your Nobility notices our patience when so long a letter was being read to us. And while he was speaking (and in another hand:
passages.notes: The first sentence is obscure: perhaps "let our patience count as much as their letter". Scanning errors corrected: "postra", "epistota", "sip", "Anhnadvertit nobilius".

passages.original: 265. Augustinus episcopus Ecclesiæ catholicæ dixit. 0 si esses et tu patiens donec ftniam quod prosequor! Ergo , ut dicere coeperam , divina sunt testimonia de zizaniis et tritico ea quæ intelligere conati. Verumtamen de retibus aliquando confessi sunt quod malos et bonos habitura est Ecclesia; sed eos dixerunt esse sacerdotibus incognitos, et ideo non praebonis quoniamignorarentur.
passages.english: 265. Augustine, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: O, if only you too were patient until I finish what I am setting out! So, as I had begun to say, the testimonies about the tares and the wheat are divine, those which they tried to understand [otherwise]. Nevertheless, concerning the nets, they have at times admitted that the Church will contain bad and good; but they said that these [bad ones] were unknown to the priests, and therefore did no harm to the good, since they were not known.
passages.notes: "ea quæ intelligere conati" seems incomplete. "non praebonis" read as "non obesse bonis" ("did no harm to the good").

passages.original: 272. Augustinus episcopus Ecclesiae catholicæ dixit. Ideo et illa conscripta sunt, et hæc excipiuntur. Si quid memoriam fallit, et ego possum petere ut mihi de epistola recitetur; et ipsi possunt, ut, illis cx codicibus recitetur , præbere silentium. Agamus a!i- quid. Ut ergo dicere coeperam, ipsis admonentibus, invenimus in scripturis mundi nomen in malo , mundi nomen in bono. Nam mundi nomen in malo, sicut ipsi dixerunt: Et mundus eum non cognovit (Joan.
passages.english: 272. Augustine, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: That is why those things were written down, and these are being taken down [now]. If memory fails on any point, I too can ask that the letter be read out for me; and they, for their part, can keep silent while it is read out from those books. Let us get something done. So, as I had begun to say, at their own prompting we find in the scriptures the name "world" used in a bad sense, and the name "world" used in a good sense. For the name "world" [is used] in a bad sense, as they themselves said: "And the world did not know him" (John
passages.notes: "cx codicibus" read as "ex codicibus"; "a!i- quid" as "aliquid". The clause "et ipsi possunt, ut, illis ex codicibus recitetur, praebere silentium" is awkward; rendered as "they can keep silent while it is read from those books". The text breaks off in the middle of the citation (John 1:10).

passages.original: 281. Augustinus episcopus Ecclesiæcatholicæ dixit. Mundus ergo, non enim aliter et nobis videri potuit, in hominibus intelligitur : non utique ita stulti simus ut belluas etiam et quacumque irrationa*bilia animantia ad salutem, quam Christus promisit, pertinere dicamus. Prorsus hoc dicimus : Mundus in maligno positus est : homines sunt. Ut credat mundus quia tu me misisti: homines sunt.
passages.english: 281. Augustine, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: So "the world" (for it could not seem otherwise to us either) is understood [to mean] people. Surely we should not be so foolish as to say that beasts too, and any irrational living creatures whatever, belong to the salvation which Christ promised. This is exactly what we say: "The world lies in the evil one": these are people. "That the world may believe that you sent me": these are people.
passages.notes: "in maligno positus est" (1 John 5:19) may be read "in the evil one" or "in evil".
